item.title: Deadlock deepens: US heads toward first shutdown since 2019
item.description: The US federal government is on the brink of a shutdown after Democrats and Republicans blocked each other’s funding plans in the Senate. This partisan deadlock, driven by healthcare spending disputes, guarantees a shutdown from Wednesday, potentially furloughing hundreds of thousands of federal workers amid escalating political tensions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Say it to my face': House minority leader slams Trump; calls US president ‘racist’ over deepfake video
item.description: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries accused Donald Trump of racism over a deepfake video posted on Truth Social. The fabricated video depicted Jeffries in a sombrero with mariachi music, mocking Democrats' stance on migrant benefits. Jeffries challenged Trump to confront him directly, stating, "Say it to my face," after the video also parodied Chuck Schumer.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Student bodies warn Labour of losing Indian talent if levy imposed on foreign students
item.description: Labour's proposed levy on international students to fund domestic maintenance grants faces strong opposition from student bodies and universities. Critics warn a 6% charge risks pricing out Indian students, who contribute billions, and could lead to significant financial losses for UK universities, ultimately harming the sector and even domestic student access.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Canton

item.title: Government shutdown: From banks to courts- What stays open and what closes if Senate fails to pass funding bills
item.description: The United States faces a government shutdown by Tuesday midnight. President Trump and Congress are deadlocked over a spending bill. Hundreds of thousands of federal employees could face furloughs. Trump also threatens permanent layoffs. Food aid, postal service, and federal law enforcement will continue operations. National parks and museums may close. Both parties trade blame for the impasse.

item.title: 'Tariff is my favourite word': Trump says US getting 'rich as hell'; mocks critics
item.description: President Donald Trump declared "tariff" his favorite word, asserting it made the US "rich as hell." He voiced concern over a Supreme Court challenge to his tariff policy, which he believes has generated trillions. Trump also criticized "fake news" for mocking his word choice, leading him to reclassify "tariff" as his fifth favorite.

item.title: VOA job cuts paused: Judge blocks Trump administration layoffs of over 500 staff; cites ‘concerning disrespect’
item.description: A US federal judge has temporarily blocked the Trump administration's plan to cut 532 jobs at Voice of America (VOA), citing concerns over the broadcaster's mission. Judge Royce Lamberth sharply criticised the administration for "concerning disrespect" and "obfuscation," warning of potential contempt proceedings. This ruling preserves the status quo, preventing immediate layoffs at the government-funded news agency.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Charlie Kirk assassination: From understaffed security to weak monitoring - how security gaps left MAGA activist vulnerable
item.description: Charlie Kirk was shot dead at Utah Valley University. The incident exposed significant campus security lapses. An outdoor venue, minimal police presence, and no drone monitoring contributed to the vulnerability. The university's public safety resources lagged behind its rapid growth. This raises serious questions about campus preparedness across the nation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dubai Holding, Brookfield Properties launch 234 exclusive beachfront homes in the heart of Dubai
item.description: Dubai Holding Investments and Brookfield Properties have launched Solaya, a 40-acre beachfront development in Jumeirah 1 offering 234 luxury residences. Designed by Foster + Partners and 1508 London, Solaya blends elegant architecture with wellness-focused amenities like a spa, fitness center, and private cinema. This project marks a new chapter in their strategic partnership, reinforcing Dubai’s reputation for world-class living.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pumped and dumped Pakistan back in US favor; Trump says he loved Pak general thanking him for saving millions of lives
item.description: US President Donald Trump reiterated his claim of averting nuclear war between India and Pakistan, praising Pakistani leaders for their gratitude. He also repeated unsubstantiated claims of seven downed planes. Trump's admiration for Pakistan's "Field Marshal" and their Middle-East peace plan support signals renewed US-Pakistan ties, despite some analysts' caution.
item.dc:creator: Chidanand Rajghatta

item.title: 'Enemy within': Trump drops mask, tells US military to quell civil disturbances; says will fire generals he doesn't like
item.description: US President Donald Trump threatened to fire military leaders he disliked. He declared a 'war from within' against crime and immigration. Trump warned the military would assist in crackdowns on Democratic-run cities. He ordered a quick reaction force for civil disturbances. Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth criticized 'woke' policies. Hegseth mandated fitness tests and new grooming standards for all military personnel. He stressed the need for fit officers.

item.title: 'We'll see how it is': Donald Trump gives Hamas 3-4 days to accept Gaza 'peace plan'; warns of 'sad end' if rejected
item.description: US President Donald Trump issued a 3-4 day ultimatum for Hamas to accept a Gaza peace proposal, co-presented with Israeli PM Netanyahu. The plan demands Hamas disarm in exchange for a ceasefire, aid, and reconstruction, with Trump warning of severe consequences for refusal. Hamas stated it will study the internationally backed proposal before responding.

item.title: ‘Fat generals, admirals unacceptable’: Pete Hegseth convenes meet with US military officials; directives given on fitness, ‘woke culture'
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth convened a secret meeting at Quantico to unveil sweeping directives, including implementing gender-neutral physical fitness standards and eliminating "woke" culture from the military. He emphasized physical fitness, reformed personnel records, and warned dissenting leaders to resign, drawing scrutiny for the meeting's urgency and secrecy amid broader military changes.

item.title: What Abu Dhabi parents must know about the 2025 School Transport Policy: No solo travel for kids under 15
item.description: Abu Dhabi has updated its school transport policy for 2025–26, focusing on student safety, clear responsibilities for parents, and improved communication. Key changes include rules for independent travel, adult supervision for younger students, regulated bus fees, and real-time tracking through the Salama app. Parents are required to submit consent forms and follow all procedures set by schools and authorities.
